title: Opal quant heuristic scan — field memo
content:
Summary:

This note captures a compact field-style sweep we ran on the cluster to probe heuristics for kernel selection between INT8, FP8, GPTQ and AWQ variants. Goal: find low-risk mitigation steps for observed tail-latency jitter on long-context workloads and produce a lightweight playbook for runtime kernel routing.

High-level takeaways (short):
- AWQ delivers the highest steady-state throughput for short- to mid-length sequences but shows p99 spikes under bursty long-context traffic.
- INT8 kernels are stable across workloads but require per-layer scale tuning to avoid quality cliff (not throughput cliff) on some attention patterns.
- FP8 has competitive throughput and lower memory footprint vs GPTQ but shows deterministic artefacts for sparse-attention-like prompts (rare in prod but reproducible).
- GPTQ variants give better output fidelity for aggressive compression but cost more memory and slightly higher p50 latency on our vectorized kernels.
- Microprofiling points to L2/L3 misses and dispatcher serialization as the dominant root causes for the p99 AWQ spikes.

Experiment setup:
- Hardware: 8x A100-80GB (server-level cluster), mixed PCIe topology (4 GPUs per socket, NVLink mesh) — tests pinned to a single GPU to avoid inter-GPU noise, except one multi-GPU burst test.
- Models: 7B and 13B families (same architecture), baseline float32 fp32 reference.
- Quant variants: INT8 (per-channel symmetric), FP8 (e4m3-like emulation), GPTQ (per-layer tuned), AWQ (per-group adaptive).
- Kernels: vector-macro (SIMD-focused), tiled-matrix (cache-aware), fused-attn (attention-optimized).
- Traffic: synthetic replay of customer burst traces (mixture of short chat messages and long context summarization requests), 30m warmup then 15m steady, 2h extended burst run for tail analysis.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU SM occupancy, L2/L3 miss rates, KV cache hit rate, dispatch queue length, memory allocated, and model token accuracy on a 50-prompt diff set.

What we measured (high level numbers, 13B model):
- Throughput (tokens/sec, mid-phase): AWQ+vector: 1520 t/s, INT8+vector: 1280 t/s, FP8+tiled: 1410 t/s, GPTQ+fused-attn: 1345 t/s.
- Latency medians (ms per request): AWQ: 28ms, INT8: 32ms, FP8: 30ms, GPTQ: 33ms.
- Tail (p99) during long-context bursts: AWQ p99 jumped to 420ms intermittently; others stayed under 220ms.
- Quality regressions (perplexity-like proxy on 50-prompt set): AWQ delta +0.7 relative to fp32; GPTQ +0.2; INT8 +0.9 but concentrated on 6/50 prompts with attention-sparse patterns; FP8 +1.4 on 4/50 prompts (visible token skew).

Profiling notes and root cause hypotheses:
1) Dispatcher serialization and kernel microbursts
- Flame traces show that AWQ kernels trigger intermittent long-running fused kernels that briefly block the dispatcher queue. When concurrent short requests arrive while a long fused kernel runs, queue length grows and latency spikes appear.
- Hypothesis: AWQ's per-group dynamic packing leads to occasional oversized GEMM dimensions that increase kernel runtime variance.

2) Cache-line alignment & KV cache eviction interactions
- In long-context sequences, KV cache is large; AWQ packing changes memory layout slightly and causes more frequent L2 cache misses during KV reads. Profiling counters show a 1.6x increase in L2 misses on AWQ vs INT8 in the same workload slice.
- Hypothesis: slight shift in memory alignment for attention indices triggers pathological access patterns on tiled kernels.

3) Kernel configuration fragmentation
- We observed many tiny configuration switches between kernel flavors inside the same request (especially when sequence length crosses boundaries). Each switch flushes small internal buffers and causes inefficient kernel launches.
- Hypothesis: heuristics that pick kernel based strictly on sequence-length buckets are too brittle for mixed-batch traffic.

Actionable mitigations we tried (and results):
- Padding heuristic: add 4 tokens of padding (zeroed) for requests whose sequence length is within 5 tokens of a kernel boundary. Result: reduced AWQ p99 spikes by ~45% in replayed traces (did not affect output quality in our checks).
- Soft-routing cooldown: avoid switching kernel flavor more than once per request lifecycle; keep kernel pinned for full request. Result: cut dispatch thrash by ~30% and reduced queue jitter.
- KV prefetch smoothing: when long-context requests are detected, pre-warm KV pages on upcoming kernels to reduce initial L2 miss storm. Result: modest p99 improvement, but requires small memory reservation and increases cold-start cost.
- Group-size clamp for AWQ: limit max group packing to avoid oversized GEMMs. Result: throughput dropped ~8% but p99 improved significantly; suggestion: enable clamp for latency-SLO customers.

Open anomalies we couldn't fully explain:
- On one host, AWQ p99 spikes correlated with a background host process that caused PCIe interrupts; reproducible on that host only. Likely infra noise, not kernel.
- FP8 deterministic artefacts: token-level diffs show repeated token insertions for prompts with block-sparse attention patterns. We couldn't find a simple per-layer scale fix; may need a fallback to higher-precision attention for affected layers.

Playbook recommendations (short checklist for runtime):
- Default kernel routing: prefer INT8 vectorized for stability, AWQ vector for cost-sensitive short-context workloads.
- For customers with p99 < 200ms SLO: enable AWQ clamp + padding heuristic + soft-routing cooldown.
- For long-context-heavy workloads: prefer tiled or fused-attn GPTQ to balance fidelity and tail.
- Add profiling triggers: when p99 > 2x baseline, capture per-request kernel switch log, KV miss histogram, and dispatcher queue snapshot. Upload to /rt-profiles for triage.
- Add a lightweight A/B flag to route subset of traffic to the mitigations above for 24–72h before full rollout.

Next experiments to run (priority):
1) Systematic group-size x batchshape sweep for AWQ to quantify the throughput vs p99 Pareto curve. (owner: Diego)
2) FP8 local patch to attention rescaling in sparse-like patterns (owner: Priya)
3) Larger multi-GPU noisy-host test to verify infra-correlated PCIe interrupt hypothesis (owner: SRE / Jonah)
4) Long-run stability test (7-day) with padding heuristic and clamp enabled to measure cumulative quality drift. (owner: Maya)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a field-style memo: experiments were compact, not yet full orthogonal grid sweeps. Numbers are representative of our cluster slice and should be validated at scale.
- If you want the raw traces and perf counters, see the linked PR and RDW ticket above. We also have flame graphs saved under rt-profiles/opal-scan/ (ask Diego for access).

Appendix — quick commands and artifacts:
- repro harness: scripts/perf/opal_scan/run_replay.sh --model 13B --variant AWQ --kernel vector --trace traces/burst_2026-02-02.json
- upload: ./tools/rt-upload --path rt-profiles/opal-scan/2026-02-10 --include counters,flame,kv-hist

End of memo.
